title: CNS cell NER extractor output
description: Output shape for prompts/extractor-ner-cns-cells.md. A cell-specific superset of ner-output.schema.json: same source_metadata / entities / key_terms / entities_grouped / stats contract, plus the cell label taxonomy, the cell_context block, and the annotation conventions a human gold standard follows (specificity, coordinated mention slots, SKOS-qualified ontology_id). Kept as its own file so ner-output.schema.json stays task-agnostic. Standalone by design — the sibling schemas do not cross-$ref either, so any validator works without a resolver. See references/cell-annotation-conventions.md.

source_metadata.description: Document-level metadata. Populated ONCE per run, not per item.

entities.description: Raw mentions — one item per occurrence (exhaustive). Nested spans are LEGAL and expected here: a hedged wrapper and the groundable term inside it usually share a start offset and differ only in end. Do not de-overlap them.

entities_grouped.description: Per-entity index — mentions collapsed by canonical (entity.lower(), label). Attached by scripts/group_by_entity.py.

ensemble_models.description: Per-model summary from the NER ensemble run (--ner-profile cns_cells). Records which models contributed and which were skipped.

label.description: For LLM-extracted items this is closed to the cns-cells taxonomy (see the allOf rule below) because the prompt says do not invent labels. It stays open for HF-ensemble items: scripts/ner_models.py normalises what it can and passes unrecognised model labels through verbatim, and the cns_cells profile legitimately emits Anatomy / Gene / CellLine / Disease, which are not in the cns-cells taxonomy at all.

specificity.description: Cell items only (CellClass / CellType / CellSubtype / CellOntologyTerm); omit or null for BrainRegion, LineageMarker and the rest. cell_phenotype = identity stated well enough to ground. cell_vague = a hedged set ('<TYPE> subtypes', 'subsets of …', or '<MARKER>+ cells' naming no type) — a marker does NOT make a cell type. cell_hetero = a deliberate mixture, or a negatively-defined set ('non-<MARKER>+ cells'). vague and hetero items are correct output, not failures.

coordinated_elements.description: How many distinct cells this span names; 1 unless the span is a conjunction ('A and B cells' → 2). ontology_id then carries exactly this many ';'-separated slots, in text order, with '-' for a slot that has no ontology term. A missing '-' shifts every later mapping by one.

cell_context.description: Attributes co-mentioned with this cell. Populated on cell items; the co-mentioned attributes are ALSO emitted as their own entities (see the prompt's ephys/marker rules) — this block is the tie-back, not a substitute.

source_model.description: Which model surfaced this mention. HF model id (e.g. 'pruas/BENT-PubMedBERT-NER-Cell-Type'), or 'llm_ner:<llm_model>'. In host-model mode this is your own model id — see SKILL.md rule 16.

source_score.description: The source model's own confidence (0–1) if it emits one (HF NER models do; LLM extractors usually don't).

ontology_id.description: Ontology IRI/CURIE, optionally SKOS-qualified: '(skos:exact)' when the mention IS the class, '(skos:related)' when it is near — a derived or reporter-line population, a marker-narrowed subset, or a tissue term standing in for its cells. Exactness depends on the paper, not the string. Two separators, NOT interchangeable: ';' separates coordinated mentions (one slot per coordinated_elements, '-' for a gap), ',' separates multiple candidate IRIs for a SINGLE mention.

concept_mapping_provenance.description: 'llm_knowledge' is forbidden in canonical output and is demoted to 'unmapped' by scripts/iri_validation.py (rule 15). Fabricated CL terms are worse than an honest 'unmapped'.

then.description: A vague mention names no cell type, so there is nothing to ground. Any ontology_id here is a fabrication.

LLM-extracted (or not-yet-tagged) items must use the cns-cells taxonomy — the prompt forbids inventing labels. HF-ensemble items are exempt: ner_models.py passes unrecognised model labels through verbatim, and the cns_cells profile emits Anatomy / Gene / CellLine / Disease by design.

EntityGroup.description: An entity index entry: one canonical (entity, label) with all mentions collapsed.

consensus_count.description: Distinct source_models that surfaced this entity. Useful as a confidence proxy.

specificity.description: Carried up when every mention in the group agrees. Leave null when they disagree — the same surface form can be phenotype in one sentence and part of a hedged set in another, and that disagreement is signal, not noise.

mentions.description: Slim per-occurrence views (offsets, sentence, source_model, judge_score).
